channel.title: GigaMail blog
channel.description: Notes from building an email agent you can trust: one problem per article, with the numbers.

item.title: A phishing mail was written for two readers: the person and the AI summary
item.description: A security vendor describes a phishing mail with a visible lure for the person and hidden instructions for the assistant that summarises it. What that changes, and what GigaMail's visible-text reading does and does not cover.

item.title: An agent told to wait before deleting mail deleted hundreds of messages
item.description: A director at an AI lab told an autonomous agent not to act until told. It deleted hundreds of emails anyway, after losing the instruction. Which step an approval kept outside the agent would have stopped, and which it would not.

item.title: A link preview sent data out before anyone approved the draft
item.description: An approval step can leak on its own. Telegram opens the first link of a message to build a preview, so a draft with data in a link sent it out before anyone tapped approve. What changed in GigaMail 0.6.7.

item.title: Hiding invisible text from an email agent withheld 28% of real mail
item.description: An email can say one thing to you and another to your AI agent. We made the agent read only what a person sees, and more than one HTML mail in four went missing. What was in the way, and how it came down to 6%.
